title: Thomson Reserve launch sales hit over 90% or 1,143 units at average of $2,900 psf
article:
Thomson Reserve , the first mega private residential development with over 1,000 units launched this year, saw 1,143 of its 1,268 units (90.1%) sold over the VIP preview on Oct 30 and launch day on Oct 31.

The units were sold at an average price of $2,900 psf, according to a joint statement by developers UOL Group and CapitaLand Development (CLD).

The sales make it the top-selling new condo launch of 2026 by number of units sold. It also marks the highest launch sales volume since ParkTown Residence in Tampines North sold 1,041 of its 1,193 units (87%) in February 2025.

Both developments are joint ventures between UOL Group, its subsidiary Singapore Land Group (SingLand), and CLD.

According to sources, demand was strong across all unit types, particularly for larger apartments. All 350 three-bedroom and 174 four-bedroom units were sold, along with 26 of the 28 five-bedroom suites.

The four- and five-bedroom units were released during VIP bookings on Friday, Oct 30, and were almost entirely snapped up ahead of the official launch on Saturday.

All 200 two-bedroom-plus-study units were also sold.

The highest absolute price achieved was said to be $5.98 million ($3,306 psf) for a 1,808 sq ft five-bedroom suite on the 30th floor of the Luxury Collection, after a 6% + 2% discount.

Meanwhile, the highest psf price was $3,334 psf for a four-bedroom premium unit that fetched $4.56 million, also after a 6% + 2% discount.

The strong sales followed a record turnout of 32,000 visitors over two weekends of public preview. Thomson Reserve also collected more than 3,300 cheques ahead of the launch, representing a subscription rate of over 2.6 times.

According to the developers, the majority of buyers were Singaporeans purchasing for owner-occupation and investment.

“The robust take-up reflects buyers’ confidence in Thomson Reserve’s distinctive proposition and strong product positioning,” says a spokesperson on behalf of the joint venture in a statement.

They attributed the project's appeal to its spacious, upscale homes, connectivity, proximity to reputable schools and nature parks, and the popular Upper Thomson dining stretch.

The 99-year leasehold development is located at Bright Hill Drive, off Upper Thomson Road, with a sheltered walkway connecting it to Upper Thomson MRT Station on the Thomson-East Coast Line.

title: Top Stock Market Highlights of the Week: Anthropic’s IPO Filing, Intel, Alphabet and Microsoft
article:
It was a turbulent week for technology investors.
One of the world’s most closely watched
artificial intelligence
(AI) developers took its first formal step towards a public listing.
Meanwhile, results from three US tech heavyweights showed how the cost of the AI arms race is starting to weigh on earnings and balance sheets.
Alphabet
(NASDAQ: GOOGL) suffered a historic sell-off, Intel’s guidance disappointed, and
Microsoft
(NASDAQ: MSFT) turned to the bond market to fund its build-out.
AI developer files for a Nasdaq listing
Anthropic, the AI company behind the Claude chatbot, filed a registration statement on Form S-1 with the US Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) on 26 October 2026 for a proposed initial public offering (IPO).
The company intends to list its Class A common stock on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the symbol “ANT” (proposed NASDAQ: ANT).
The number of shares to be offered and the price range have not yet been determined.
Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley are named as contacts for the preliminary prospectus.
The registration statement has not yet become effective, so no shares can be sold until the SEC process is complete.
The filing comes as Anthropic’s influence on listed tech giants grows.
This week, Microsoft cited heavy demand from Anthropic and OpenAI as a driver of its capital spending.
Rival chatbots such as Claude have also been cited as a headwind for Google’s search business.
Investors will be watching for the full prospectus, which should give the first detailed look at Anthropic’s revenue, losses and growth.
Chipmaker sinks as PC slump and supply snags cloud outlook
Intel Corporation
(NASDAQ: INTC) shares fell about 15% in after-hours trading on 29 October 2026 after its guidance fell short of expectations.
The chipmaker expects revenue for the fourth quarter of 2026 (4Q2026) of US$15 billion to US$16 billion, below the analyst average of US$17 billion.
It guided for adjusted earnings per share (EPS) of US$0.25, against estimates of US$0.43.
Gross margin is projected to narrow from 43% to 38%.
The guidance overshadowed a solid third quarter of 2026 (3Q2026).
Revenue rose 21% year on year (YoY) to US$16.5 billion, and EPS of US$0.52 beat forecasts of US$0.41.
The data centre grew 78% YoY to US$7.3 billion.
The client division, which makes PC chips, slipped 5% to US$8.1 billion.
CEO Tan Lip-Bu blamed soaring memory chip prices, which have hurt PC shipments.
He expects the PC market to shrink by 10% in 2027, following a 12% decline in 2026.
Raw material shortages and a factory shutdown in Israel also constrained supply.
The sell-off comes after Intel’s share price more than doubled in 2026.
Search giant suffers worst day on record
Alphabet
shares plunged 13% on 29 October 2026, wiping out roughly US$500 billion in market value.
It was the steepest one-day fall since Google’s 2004 listing, surpassing the previous record decline of 11.63% set in March 2020.
The trigger was the group’s 3Q2026 report, released after the US market closed on 28 October.
Alphabet posted negative free cash flow of US$9.07 billion, against the US$2.7 billion analysts had expected.
It was the second consecutive quarter of negative free cash flow.
It kept its full-year capital expenditure guidance at US$195 billion to US$205 billion.
Search advertising, its largest revenue source, grew 12% YoY to US$63.35 billion but missed estimates.
Chief business officer Philipp Schindler attributed part of the shortfall to lower monetisation within Google’s AI Mode.
He added that the company is now scaling ads across its AI products.
Not every analyst is concerned.
Rosenblatt Securities analyst Scott Devitt argued that Google’s base of around four billion search users leaves it well placed once AI search monetisation matures.
Software giant taps bond market to fund AI ambitions
Microsoft announced on 29 October 2026 that it will raise US$25 billion in bonds to fund its infrastructure expansion, drawing on its top-tier AAA credit rating from S&P.
The offerings are expected to close on 4 November.
Management is targeting US$170 billion in capital expenditure for 2026 to meet
heavy demand
from AI labs such as Anthropic and OpenAI.
In its latest quarter, capital expenditure and finance leases totalled US$45.2 billion.
That was 30% higher YoY but below the US$50.67 billion analysts had projected.
Free cash flow fell 27% YoY to US$18.63 billion but remained positive.
That sets Microsoft apart from Alphabet,
Meta Platforms
(NASDAQ: META) and
Amazon
(NASDAQ: AMZN), which have all reported negative free cash flow.
Chief financial officer Amy Hood said Microsoft has so far relied on leasing and its own cash generation.
Microsoft will tap debt markets when conditions are attractive.
Investors, however, have grown more cautious towards heavily indebted companies as central banks raise interest rates to fight inflation.

title: China's graft agency probes ex-Sinopec chairman Fu Chengyu
article:
(Oct 31): Fu Chengyu, the former chairman of China Petrochemical Corp (Sinopec), is under investigation for suspected serious violations of discipline and law, China’s top anti-graft agency said on Saturday.

Fu is undergoing a disciplinary review and supervisory investigation by the Central Commission for Discipline Inspection and the National Supervisory Commission, according to a statement on the agency’s website.

Fu Chengyu, born in 1951, is a veteran of China’s oil industry who led China National Offshore Oil Corporation before becoming the chairman and Communist Party chief of Sinopec in 2011. He departed Sinopec in May 2015 after reaching retirement age.

title: Bank of England may raise high-risk mortgage threshold, FT says
article:
(Oct 31): The Bank of England is considering easing restrictions on higher-risk mortgage loans in a move that could support the UK housing market, the Financial Times (FT) reported.

Under pressure from lenders and the government, the central bank’s Financial Policy Committee (FPC) is examining whether to increase a key lending threshold to five times borrowers’ household income, up from 4.5 times at present, the newspaper said. Since 2014, most banks have been prevented from offering more than 15% of mortgages to borrowers above that loan-to-income level.

The Bank of England told the FT that it “keeps its housing tools under regular review, having regard to the FPC’s primary and secondary objectives”.

According to the FT, the bank lobby group UK Finance estimates that raising the threshold could free up additional lending capacity equivalent to 7% of new residential mortgages.

The UK residential property market is under renewed pressure as surging mortgage costs squeeze prospective buyers. House prices stagnated in October, according to one of the country’s largest mortgage lenders, following a 0.3% decline in September.

UK Chancellor John Healey wrote to the Bank of England this week, urging the FPC to “target improving access to home ownership without prejudicing financial stability” and to consider how the loan-to-income threshold can better support that objective.

See also: Britain’s plan to tax its way out of debt tests the limits

That followed his move in Wednesday’s budget to double the UK’s bank tax surcharge to 6%, raising roughly £1.5 billion (US$2 billion or $2.6 billion) to help fund cost-of-living relief for cash-strapped households.

title: OpenAI’s Altman meets Samsung executives as chip crunch deepens
article:
(Oct 31): OpenAI chief executive officer Sam Altman met with Samsung Group’s top executives in South Korea on Saturday to deepen cooperation on memory chips and artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure as global shortages intensify.

Samsung hosted Altman for talks with about 50 executives from its electronics, financial and biotechnology affiliates in Yongin, south of Seoul, the South Korean company said in a statement. The discussions focused on how AI can reshape industries, corporate decision-making and business opportunities over the next decade.

The meeting comes as shortages in a broad array of memory products strain the global electronics industry and send chip prices soaring. Demand from data-centre operators is intensifying competition for supplies, with the five biggest players in the AI infrastructure race planning to spend more than US$3 trillion ($3.8 trillion) in the coming years. Memory accounts for roughly a third of data-centre spending.

Altman is the latest American tech leader to visit South Korea, the leader in advanced memory chips and a country where AI adoption is accelerating among businesses and consumers. Nvidia Corp CEO Jensen Huang and Advanced Micro Devices Inc's Lisa Su both visited twice since last year to strengthen supply-chain ties. Technology executives have warned that chip production is struggling to keep pace with demand.

Saturday’s meeting builds on a partnership announced earlier to supply memory chips for OpenAI’s Stargate infrastructure project and cooperate on AI data centres, including floating offshore facilities. Samsung is also accelerating AI adoption across its businesses, from research and manufacturing to marketing and corporate operations.

title: OpenAI funding target cut by US$10 bil as AI slumps — report
article:
(Oct 31): OpenAI has cut its fundraising target by US$10 billion ($12.8 billion) as an AI stock sell-off and rival Anthropic PBC’s impending public listing complicate its efforts to secure investor commitments, the Financial Times (FT) reported.

The ChatGPT maker is now seeking about US$20 billion at a US$1.25 trillion valuation, down from US$30 billion at a US$1.4 trillion valuation last month, the FT said, citing people with knowledge of the matter.

Some investors have reduced their commitments to OpenAI’s funding round, according to the report. The scaled-back ambitions reflect growing investor unease over the enormous sums being poured into artificial intelligence (AI). The Nasdaq 100 fell 3.5% on Friday.

Bloomberg News reported last week that OpenAI was seeking to raise capital at a US$1.25 trillion valuation during the final stages of negotiations.

A group of investors from the United Arab Emirates, including state-backed MGX, is expected to be the largest participant in the round, the FT said. SoftBank Group Corp and venture capital firms including Sequoia Capital, Coatue Management, Founders Fund and Andreessen Horowitz also plan to participate, according to the report.

OpenAI, Sequoia, Founders Fund and SoftBank declined to comment, the report said. MGX, Coatue and Andreessen Horowitz did not immediately respond to a request for comments, according to the FT.

See also: Amazon taps US$80 bil supplier loan facility to help fund AI

The fundraising effort faces additional competition from Anthropic, which is preparing to go public next month at a valuation of at least US$1.5 trillion, the newspaper said. OpenAI, which raised US$122 billion in March, is seeking fresh capital to finance its vast computing ambitions as it prepares for a potential initial public offering of its own next year, according to the report.

title: DHLT to divest DPL Sendai Port for JPY13.5 bil; to acquire DPL Hiroshima Itsukaichi Port for JPY8.2 bil
article:
The manager of Daiwa House Logistics Trust (DHLT) has announced an asset recycling plan on Oct 30 which the REIT will be divesting DPL Sendai Port to its Sponsor, Daiwa House Industry, and to acquire DPL Hiroshima Itsukaichi Port from an independent third party.

The divestment consideration of DPL Sendai Port is at JPY13.5 billion ($110 million), which represent a premium of 2.7% above the average of the two independent valuation of JPY13.15 billion as at Sept 30.

Proceeds from the above divestment will be partially utilised for the proposed acquisition of DPL Hiroshima Itsukaichi Port, which has a price tag of JPY8.2 billion.

The JPY8.2 billion acquisition consideration represent a discount of 16.7% from the independent valuation of JPY9.9 billion as at Sept 30.

Remaining net proceeds from the divestment will be deployed towards repayment of borrowings and working capital requirements.

As laid out in its Oct 30 press release, upon completion of both proposed transactions and on a pro forma basis, DHLT’s net property income (NPI) for FY2025 and 1HFY2026 would increase by around 4% and 7.9% respectively.

See also: MLT to redevelop two adjacent Changi South properties into a Grade A warehouse for $141 mil

Distribution per Unit (DPU) would increase by 5.5% and 11% for FY2025 and 1HFY2026 respectively.

Explaining the latest move, the manager says that the divestment of DPL Sendai comes at a time where occupancy rate has declined from 100% as at Dec 31, 2024 to just 31.9% as at Sept 30.

The manager adds that DPL Sendai would see significant downtime and large capital expenditure if it were to undergoes an asset enhancement initiative (AEI). As such, the manager has conducted an exercise to determine market interest for DPL Sendai and did not receive any other offers aside from the offer from its Sponsor.

See also: Mapletree Industrial Trust to pay 2QFY2027 distribution of 2.97 cents per unit, down 6.6% y-o-y

On the other hand, DHLT sees the acquisition of DPL Hiroshima Itsukaichi Port as a “positive move” given that it is fully occupied by two large third-party logistics companies, which will improve its overall portfolio occupancy from 88.5% to 96.9% as at Sept 30, on a pro forma basis.

On a pro forma basis, DHLT’s aggregate leverage as at June 30 is expected to improve from 40.1% to 38.3% following both proposed truncations.

“We believe that in the current circumstances, the proposed transactions offer an optimal solution to the challenges faced by DPL Sendai Port. We look forward to the continual support from Unitholders,” says Jun Yamamura, CEO of the manager.

Units in DHLT closed 0.5 cents higher, or up 1.23% at 41 cents on Oct 30.

title: Fed officials back more rate hikes, gradual pace of tightening
article:
(Oct 31): A trio of US Federal Reserve (Fed) officials reaffirmed the need for additional interest-rate hikes while counseling a gradual approach to tightening that would minimise disruptions to financial markets and the economy.

“It remains clear to me, given the current outlook, that the FOMC (Federal Open Market Committee) needs to implement at least two more 25-basis-point rate increases,” Dallas Fed president Lorie Logan said on Friday. “Adjusting policy more gradually can help households, businesses and market participants adapt to higher rates and reduce the risk that economic activity deteriorates more sharply than necessary.”

Logan’s speech at Davidson College, along with similar remarks from Richmond Fed president Tom Barkin and the St Louis Fed’s Alberto Musalem, followed a decision on Wednesday by the US central bank’s FOMC to leave its benchmark interest rate unchanged. The FOMC previously voted in September to raise the rate for the first time since 2023.

The Dallas Fed chief, who holds a vote on rate decisions this year, said “skipping a meeting does not change the monetary policy destination”.

Barkin, speaking in a radio interview on Friday on SiriusXM, said “a gradual approach is a good way to go”, while Musalem at an event in New York argued “incremental adjustments made earlier are usually less disruptive than larger and abrupt actions taken later”.

Most Fed officials, in projections published after the September meeting, viewed an additional rate hike this year as likely necessary. Investors now see that happening at the Fed’s last meeting of the year on Dec 8-9, according to future contracts, which also indicate they will likely opt for another pause in January and then consider a third rate hike in March.

See also: Treasuries extend monthly advance as tech giants stumble

On Wednesday, Fed chairman Kevin Warsh refrained from revealing his outlook for the economy or interest rates, but said elevated inflation is still the central bank’s main focus. He also described financial conditions as tighter following the rate hike in September, while adding that he is “unwilling and unable to call them tight”.

Friday’s remarks suggested there may be a growing consensus on the need to deliver more tightening in a gradual manner. Logan voted with the majority on this week’s decision to hold rates steady after dissenting against a similar decision in July, and Barkin will re-enter the voting ranks of the FOMC in 2027.

Still, Wednesday’s vote also saw two dissenters who instead favoured a second consecutive increase this month: Fed governor Lisa Cook and Cleveland Fed president Beth Hammack.

See also: US employment cost growth stable, stays below inflation

The central bank is seeking to bring down inflation that has been above its 2% target for more than five years. Data published on Thursday showed the Fed’s preferred measure accelerated to 3.6% in September amid a renewed rise in oil prices.

A separate report on Thursday also indicated the economy expanded in the third quarter at the fastest pace in a year on strength in consumer spending and business investment, which is being driven by the boom in spending related to artificial intelligence.

“If we do see a continued surge in demand, that would be the kind of thing you might want to lean against,” Barkin said.

Logan said that after the two additional rate increases she is projecting, the Fed should pause to assess economic and financial developments, and to determine whether further hikes are necessary.

“The end goal should be to make policy modestly restrictive so we can sustainably deliver both maximum employment and stable prices,” she said.

title: Trump says US looking at whether Binance hack was by North Korea
article:
(Oct 31): President Donald Trump said the US is looking into whether North Korean hackers were behind a US$6.3 billion ($8.1 billion) heist targeting Binance that has rattled the cryptocurrency world.

“We don’t know. We are looking at that,” Trump told reporters on Friday in the Oval Office when asked if the hack should be attributed to actors from North Korea.

Hackers from that country have been known to prey on the digital asset industry and accused by the FBI and cybersecurity experts of involvement in some of the biggest crypto thefts in recent years.

Binance, the world’s largest crypto trading platform, suspended withdrawals and pledged to cover all losses after the hack, the biggest heist the digital-asset industry has ever faced. Binance posted on X that about US$3 billion of the assets had been frozen on blockchain networks. In another post, co-founder Yi He said withdrawals are expected to resume by Sunday.

“They are saying they are guaranteeing it or something,” Trump said. “It was a hack. That’s the problem. You know the old-fashioned way when you used to sign a cheque, take it out. These are different people. Never see the money anymore. So I have always felt it was a little bit dangerous.”

“They say they have it pretty much under control,” he added, referring to Binance.

See also: Binance estimates US$6.3 bil hacked in crypto's biggest heist

Binance has had ties to businesses connected to the president and his family. The firm helped develop a stablecoin for a company that Trump and his sons co-founded. Changpeng Zhao, Binance’s co-founder and former chief executive officer, was pardoned by Trump in 2025 after he pleaded guilty to failing to enforce robust anti-money-laundering measures.

The hacking incident came amid growing concern about the risks posed by hackers in the artificial intelligence age. It also marked a setback for an industry that is keen to expand its presence in traditional finance and which has benefitted from Trump’s push to ease regulatory burdens.

Western governments have accused North Korea of fostering hacking groups and using them to bring in funds to pay for weapons programmes.

See also: Bitcoin drops below US$77,000 as Binance hack shakes crypto

Trump in recent weeks has floated new US outreach to North Korea, suggesting that a potential meeting with its leader, Kim Jong Un, could happen this year. Earlier this month, however, Trump downplayed those expectations, saying he was “not sure that anybody’s asking for a meeting”.

title: Intel suffers worst stock drop in decades on weak forecast
article:
(Oct 31): Intel Corp suffered its worst stock rout in more than four decades after the PC industry slump and supply-chain snags hurt its forecast, renewing fears about the chipmaker’s turnaround bid.

Sales in the fourth quarter will be US$15 billion ($19 billion) to US$16 billion, the chipmaker said in a statement on Thursday. Analysts on average estimated US$17 billion, and some projections topped US$18 billion, according to data compiled by Bloomberg. Profit will be 25 cents a share in the quarter, excluding certain items. Wall Street was projecting adjusted earnings of 43 cents a share.

Intel is contending with a severe slump in the personal computer market. Makers of laptops and desktops — key customers — are struggling with shortages of memory semiconductors and surging component prices. That’s cut into PC shipments and hurt demand from users. In addition, chief executive officer Lip-Bu Tan said his company’s data centre unit would have done even better if it hadn’t suffered from shortages of some raw materials and a shutdown of a factory in Israel — supply snags that the company is working hard to fix.

“I am a bit disappointed in terms of how we cannot fulfil the customer requirements,” Tan said in an interview.

As to the PC market, “one of the main challenges, basically, is memory”, he said. “Memory pricing went up a lot. I think my prediction is that in 2027 it is going to be a very severe issue to all of us. We are not alone — it’s just the whole market is impacted.”

Intel’s stock fell 29% to US$65.76 at the close Friday in New York, marking its worst decline according to records dating back to 1982.

See also: Meta’s rating outlook cut to negative by S&P on AI spending

Intel projects the PC downturn will persist through at least the first half of 2027 — with a decline of 10% next year following a 12% slide in 2026. Still, longer term, the company is optimistic about demand for its products and is increasing its spending on new equipment to boost production. It’s growing more confident it will attract orders from other chipmakers that want to use its factories to build their components, Tan said.

Intel’s stock had more than doubled this year through Thursday’s close, with investors betting that the company will emerge as a key AI beneficiary. The increasing deployment of artificial intelligence services has created demand for Intel’s general-purpose chips, allowing it an entry into a market dominated by the technology of Nvidia Corp.

“Intel’s earnings highlight the challenges the company faces in pushing its recent turnaround into a sustained recovery,” Emarketer senior analyst Asa Hiken said in a note. Though demand for server processors is booming, “Intel’s disappointing outlook shows that strong demand alone isn’t enough to overcome its near-term challenges, particularly ongoing weakness in its traditional PC business,” he said.

See also: Apple overtakes Nvidia to become world’s most valuable company

Intel has been pursuing a turnaround under Tan, who took the helm in March 2025. He has improved the chipmaker’s finances, cut jobs and attracted major outside investors — including Nvidia and the US government. More recently, the company offered new stock to further support its comeback.

Intel still is working to restore its technological leadership, something that once made it the envy of Silicon Valley. The company also is seeking major customers for its chip foundry business, which manufactures components for outside clients. Without those customers in place, Intel is stuck with expensive facilities that only produce internal products.

Intel executives said they expect spending on new plants and equipment to be about US$20 billion in 2026 — and then increase significantly next year. On a conference call with analysts, chief financial officer Dave Zinsner described 2027 as an “investment year” for Intel as it tries to improve output to meet rising demand. That will be particularly true for data centre products, he said. The company will likely not generate free cash flow in that period, Zinsner said.

In the fourth quarter, the shutdown of a plant in Israel will cost US$300 million in lost revenue. The company is anticipating a similar shortfall in the first three months of next year, Zinsner said. The factory, which experienced a fire, has been closed for two weeks but will begin running again in the next few days. Chips take about three months to go from raw silicon to finished components. A power outage while silicon wafers are inside a machine often causes them to be scrapped.

Third-quarter sales rose 21% to US$16.5 billion, in line with analysts’ average estimate. Earnings were 52 cents a share in the period, which ended Sept 26. Analysts projected 41 cents.

Intel’s data centre and AI unit had revenue of US$7.3 billion, a gain of 78%. Sales in the client division, which makes chips for personal computers, declined 5% to US$8.1 billion.

To stay ahead of Singapore and the region’s corporate and economic trends, click here for Latest Section

The mixed picture shows the effect that the AI boom has had on Intel’s business. Though data centre infrastructure is fuelling demand for Intel processors, it also has led to a shortage of memory chips — a type of semiconductor made by Samsung Electronics Co, SK Hynix Inc and Micron Technology Inc. That, in turn, has forced up the price of laptops and desktops, and reduced demand for the Intel chips that go into those products.

Intel’s foundry unit had sales of US$6.7 billion, an increase of 58% from the period a year earlier. That business is trying to compete in a market dominated by Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. The hope is to win enough outside customers to offset the massive cost of building chip factories and make Intel’s facilities more profitable.

Intel’s third-quarter gross margin, the percentage of revenue remaining after deducting the cost of production, was 43%. That benchmark shows the health of a company’s chipmaking operations in a costly and competitive industry. Intel projected the margin will narrow to 38% in the current period.

Though Intel now has enough of a financial cushion to weather downturns, such as the current PC market slump, it still needs to invest in its technology to stay competitive in the long run. It has lost market share to Advanced Micro Devices Inc in PC and server chips while also struggling to crack the lucrative AI accelerator category dominated by Nvidia.

title: Amazon taps US$80 bil supplier loan facility to help fund AI
article:
(Oct 31): Amazon.com Inc has set up supplier financing arrangements to borrow as much as US$80 billion ($102 billion) against the value of hardware it buys, the company’s latest move to preserve financial flexibility as it spends hundreds of billions on artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure.

Amazon has so far funded data centre construction and purchases of chips with the cash from its cloud-computing and retail operations, and with its biggest-ever corporate bond sales.

But it had largely avoided the sort of creative funding arrangements used by some of its rivals, including deals with investment groups to jointly finance data centre construction or to lease chips purchased by other entities. Many of those deals have focused on the Nvidia Corp chips that power most AI work and are often the single most expensive component of new data centre construction.

The secured loan facility, which Amazon disclosed in a quarterly filing after reporting earnings on Thursday, can be tapped at the company’s discretion from the beginning of 2027 through the third quarter of 2028. Lenders will get collateral rights over some of the assets purchased in connection with the facility. Amazon’s filing doesn’t specify what those assets included, and a spokesperson declined to comment.

“When we see such a really large opportunity in front of us, we are looking for ways to also responsibly fund that so that we can go as big as possible for our customers,” Amazon Web Services chief executive officer Matt Garman said in an interview on Bloomberg Television on Friday. Amazon, he said, was working with partners to “figure out how we can balance some of those cash flows as we’re really ramping up aggressively”.

On Thursday, Amazon reported a larger-than-expected increase in capital spending in its third-quarter earnings. The outlays led to a free cash outflow of US$42.4 billion during the year ended Sept 30. The shares were down about 2% at midday in New York.

See also: Nvidia CEO says ties to Singapore company in spy probe were ‘normal’

Amazon’s total spending commitments — including debt and interest, leases not yet commenced, obligations to acquire property and equipment and other line items — ballooned to US$883 billion at the end of September, up 36% from three months earlier and more than double where that figure stood at the same point in 2025.

title: China factory activity drops back into decline as growth wobbles
article:
(Oct 31): China’s factory activity shrank in October, underscoring the challenges facing policymakers as they seek to sustain an economic recovery to ensure this year’s growth target is met.

The official manufacturing purchasing managers’ index fell to 49.3 from 50.1 in September, the National Bureau of Statistics said Saturday. That compares with the median forecast of 49.9 in a Bloomberg survey of economists. A reading above 50 indicates expansion.

The non-manufacturing measure of activity in construction and services came in at 49.7, versus 50.2 in September.

The deterioration suggests the world’s second-largest economy has lost some traction at the start of the fourth quarter, following a modest rebound in the prior three months. Beijing may face more pressure to provide additional support after introducing a fresh package of targeted stimulus measures in recent weeks, as policymakers seek to keep growth on track to meet the government’s annual target of 4.5% to 5%.

The government has already dialled up policies to bolster the economy, offering more credit support for small businesses and consumers, mortgage subsidies for some homebuyers and additional bond quotas for local governments.

Construction on major infrastructure projects such as Six Networks has also been rolled out, and the authorities have signalled a willingness to introduce further measures if necessary.

See also: China lifts secrecy on new key rate, sets it below old benchmark

title: China lifts secrecy on new key rate, sets it below old benchmark
article:
(Oct 31): China announced the level of its new key rate after keeping it secret for four months, setting it below the old benchmark as the central bank takes the final steps towards making the overnight rate its main policy lever.

The rate on the overnight reverse repurchase agreements is 1.25%, compared with 1.4% on the current seven-day benchmark, according to a statement from the People’s Bank of China (PBOC) on Friday. While the PBOC hasn’t previously made public the rate at which overnight reverse repos were conducted, it was set at 1.25% during the first such operation in June, Bloomberg News reported at the time.

The central bank will start to conduct overnight reverse repo operations every day starting from Monday, and switch the seven-day reverse repo transactions to multiple rates from a single fixed one, according to the statement.

China’s 10-year government bond yield slipped to 1.63% from 1.64% just before the decision.

The timing of the announcement caught many analysts by surprise. Economists at banks including Societe Generale SA previously predicted the switch could take months, since the PBOC will likely need to gradually increase the frequency of its overnight liquidity operations.

See also: China’s mega banks report profit jumps as margins recover

“While this move is well telegraphed, the timing is a bit earlier than expected,” said Xiaojia Zhi, the head of an economist at Credit Agricole CIB.

“The PBOC could consider the switch now to help deliver lower short-end rates in the money markets,” Zhi added, possibly to dispel market unease over reports of state-owned developer Zhuhai Huafa Group Co’s missing payments on trust products.

Some investors see the transition as de facto easing, since the 1.25% rate was lower than expected when it was first adopted in late June. But the PBOC has refrained from associating the shift with looser policy, potentially out of concern that such interpretation may lead to frenzied buying in the Chinese government bond market.

See also: BYD earnings dampen hopes Chinese car stocks will reverse rout

“Although not a conventional 15 basis-point policy rate cut, the transition effectively increases interbank liquidity and lowers yields across the bond curve, all else equal,” Goldman Sachs Group Inc economists led by Andrew Tilton wrote in a note.

While a further policy rate cut “looks unlikely in the near term”, they said that “evolving domestic credit risk could increase the likelihood” of a reduction in lenders’ required reserves. And “to contain risk spillovers”, the PBOC may also opt to use its new instrument designed to help non-bank financial firms manage liquidity stress during bond sell-offs, according to Goldman’s economists.

Earlier in October, the PBOC gave the clearest signal yet of plans to revamp its toolkit by moving from the seven-day reverse repo rate to the overnight one. The change is part of a decades-long effort to reform China’s interest-rate system from a centrally planned framework, and better align the PBOC with other major central banks.

Financial News, a newspaper affiliated with the PBOC, cited economists in a report earlier this month as saying that the market shouldn’t conflate the central bank’s reform measures as a rate reduction.

The frequency of the seven-day reverse repo programme will also be reduced, with such operations conducted only during stretches like tax payment times and end of month periods, according to the latest statement.

Other tools that used to be based on the old benchmark will be linked to the overnight rate going forward, the PBOC said.

The sooner-than-expected announcement could be “a good strategy to get any further speculation out of the way”, according to Frances Cheung, the head of rate strategy at Oversea-Chinese Banking Corp (OCBC).

“Given that there will be overnight reverse repo operations daily, market participants will be comfortable relying on the overnight liquidity with rollovers, even if the liquidity demand is for a multi-day period,” she said. “Effectively, this would lower the funding costs.”

title: Meta’s rating outlook cut to negative by S&P on AI spending
article:
(Oct 31): S&P Global Ratings took an early step towards potentially downgrading Meta Platforms Inc’s credit rating within the next two years, amid growing pressure on the tech company’s balance sheet stemming from elevated spending tied to artificial intelligence (AI).

S&P lowered the outlook on Meta’s AA- credit grade to negative on Friday, according to a statement. The company’s rising leverage, a measure of debt relative to earnings, was also a key factor in the decision, the rating firm said.

“Meta’s ability to monetize its AI investments is more limited than that of its peers,” S&P said, adding that it’s not clear when its expenditures will start producing material revenue that exceeds the rising costs. The outlook “reflects uncertainty around how long capex will remain elevated and free operating cash flow will be negative”.

The decision signals S&P could downgrade the company within the next couple of years, but also means the bond grader isn’t actively considering downgrading Meta now. It comes as investors scrutinise Meta’s and other industry players’ ability to generate tangible returns from the massive investments they’ve been plowing into the AI buildout. The Nasdaq 100 fell 3.5%, briefly crossing the threshold of a technical correction on Friday, weighed down by disappointing tech earnings.

“We respectfully disagree with S&P’s assertion about Meta’s AI monetization capabilities,” company spokesperson Kamran Mumtaz said in a statement. “We see significant product and business opportunities ahead of us, supporting our very strong credit profile.”

Meta’s current AA- credit rating is the fourth-highest investment-grade score, and a one-notch downgrade would still leave it solidly in high-grade territory.

See also: Apple overtakes Nvidia to become world’s most valuable company

Still, the company has been borrowing heavily to fund its ambitions. S&P forecasts Meta’s capex will reach US$140 billion ($179 billion) this year, and accelerate to more than US$225 billion in 2027. The tech giant’s leverage could climb above 1.0 times as soon as next year, up from about 0.1 times last year, S&P said in the statement.

Earlier this month, Meta disclosed that it has more than US$800 billion in future spending commitments, with almost half tied to leases that haven’t yet begun yet, largely for data centres and energy infrastructure. Despite some hesitancy from Wall Street, which has pressed Meta on how it aims to make a return on its AI investments, company executives have doubled down on the need for future spending.

“We expect to continue investing aggressively to support both our core business and emerging AI initiatives,” chief financial officer Susan Li said during an earnings call with analysts.

See also: Indian AI firm seeks US$3 bil financing for Nvidia chips order — Bloomberg

Meta has made headway with its technology in recent months, particularly with its Muse models and personal AI agent. Chief executive officer Mark Zuckerberg and other leaders have outlined several ways the company could make money from these products, including through subscriptions, transaction fees, and potentially even by incorporating advertising, which already generates the vast majority of the company’s revenue via apps like Instagram, Facebook and WhatsApp.

The company is also developing plans for a cloud business, which could include selling access to various AI models hosted on Meta’s existing AI infrastructure or selling access to “raw” computing capacity.

title: Apple overtakes Nvidia to become world’s most valuable company
article:
(Oct 31): Apple Inc reclaimed the title of world’s most valuable company on Friday, taking the mantle from Nvidia Corp as investors seek the perceived safety of the iPhone maker amid concerns about artificial intelligence (AI) spending.

Shares of Apple fell 1.2% on Friday, resulting in a market capitalisation of US$5.03 trillion ($6.43 trillion), while Nvidia sank 4.2% to close with a valuation of US$4.93 trillion. This is the first time Apple has overtaken Nvidia since briefly doing so in late July.

Friday’s sell-off came as a number of major technology companies disappointed with their results, including Intel Corp and Amazon.com Inc, which followed similarly disappointing reports from Alphabet Inc and Meta Platforms Inc, among others. The reports renewed concerns about the outlook for AI spending, something Apple has largely foregone.

Fears that heavy spending on AI computing infrastructure won’t pay off have helped make Apple, which has kept a lid on capital expenditures, by far the best performing of the Magnificent Seven tech giants this year. Its shares are up 27% in 2026, more than twice the gain of second place Nvidia, which is a key beneficiary of AI spending.

The outlays have gotten so large that companies like Alphabet Inc and Amazon.com Inc have seen their free cash flow turn negative, forcing them to increasingly turn to debt markets for funding. Meanwhile, rising interest rates are raising the cost of borrowing.

See also: Indian AI firm seeks US$3 bil financing for Nvidia chips order — Bloomberg

Apple, by contrast, is projected to see its free cash flow climb 38% to US$142 billion in fiscal 2026, which ended on Sept 30.

The tech-heavy Nasdaq 100 Index fell 6.7% in October, its worst month since March 2025. CoreWeave Inc and Nebius Group, data centre owners that offer AI computing services, have dropped more than 30% this month. With Friday’s collapse, Intel lost more than 45% in October, its biggest ever one-month drop in data compiled by Bloomberg going back more than 40 years.

title: Stocks slump as Wall Street gets AI wake-up call
article:
(Oct 30): Wall Street got a reality check as a bruising sell-off in technology shares fuelled concern the artificial-intelligence (AI) frenzy that has powered the equity bull market might be overblown.

Disappointing tech results spurred the worst drop for stocks since June, with the Nasdaq 100 sinking 3.5% and briefly crossing the threshold of a technical correction. Intel Corp slid the most in over four decades. The S&P 500 fell 1.8%, breaching its 100-day moving average.

S&P Global Ratings took an early step towards potentially downgrading Meta Platforms Inc’s credit rating within the next two years, amid growing pressure on its balance sheet stemming from elevated spending tied to AI.

Apple Inc reclaimed the title of world’s most valuable company, taking the mantle from Nvidia Corp as investors seek the perceived safety of the iPhone maker amid concerns about AI spending.

The core businesses of America’s tech giants — the advertising, consumer and retail machines propping up a collective US$750 billion ($959 billion) in AI spending this year — are starting to show signs of slowing.

“The revelation that these hyperscalers are seeing a slowdown in their core businesses means that the big payoff that everyone has been saying will come eventually is getting pushed even further down the road,” said Matt Maley at Miller Tabak.

See also: At the crossroads and in the crosshairs

While AI demand remains robust, there’s a rising risk of mid-cycle capital expenditures indigestion, according to Ulrike Hoffmann-Burchardi at UBS Chief Investment Office.

“We continue to see scope for equity gains overall and believe investors should focus on building a resilient portfolio that includes exposure beyond tech,” she said.

Looking ahead, Maley noted that the biggest problem investors will face is that the rotation that has held up the US stock market could easily disappear.

See also: Stock sell-off deepens on tech earnings, bonds rise

“If the major averages begin to drop in a more compelling manner, it is very likely that investors will stop rotating into other sectors and start rotating into cash,” he said.

Elsewhere, a burst of selling hit crypto as Binance revealed a record hack that renewed questions about the security of customer assets. Higher oil prices added to anxiety amid speculation the US may resume strikes against Iran. While Treasuries barely budged Friday, they saw a solid month.
• Amazon.com Inc has set up supplier financing arrangements to borrow as much as US$80 billion against the value of hardware it buys, the company’s latest move to preserve financial flexibility as it spends hundreds of billions on artificial intelligence infrastructure.
• Alphabet Inc’s Google is in talks with the US Defense Department to work on a new data security effort underpinning the US$185 billion Golden Dome missile defence programme, according to people familiar with the matter.
• ExxonMobil Holdings Corp and Chevron Corp beat profit expectations as conflicts in the Persian Gulf and Russia roiled energy markets, driving refining results to record highs.
• Starbucks Corp chief executive officer Brian Niccol said building a multi-brand company is a possibility, two weeks after the chain shut down rumours that it was exploring a takeover of Chipotle Mexican Grill Inc.

Some of the main moves in markets:
• The S&P 500 fell 1.8% as of 4pm New York time
